facts: Sanjay Kumar and Another v State of Madhya Pradesh
Cr.A. No. 229 of 1993 (Arising out of S.L.P. (Cr.) No. 2741 of 1992)
The trial court had acquitted the appellants but the High Court convicted them under Section 307 IPC and sentenced them to rigorous imprisonment for three years.
issues: Whether the High Court was right in attributing an intention to cause death
Whether the offence fell within the ambit of Section 307 IPC
petitioner_arguments: All the six incised wounds were not more than 1/2 inch in size and were skin deep
The High Court was not right in attributing an intention to cause death
respondent_arguments: A sharp cutting instrument was used and certain injuries were caused on the chest portion of the complainant-PW 2, the intention of the assailant was clearly to commit murder
court_reasoning: The circumstances under which the incident occurred do not permit such an inference
There was no motive whatsoever. There could be no intention to kill
To justify a conviction under this provision an intention or knowledge to constitute murder must exist
The injuries caused are only skin deep and having regard to the size of the injuries it would not be permissible to infer that the assault was launched with such intent
holding: The appeal will stand disposed of accordingly
The conviction and sentence are set aside and the appellants will stand acquitted as the matter has been compounded with the permission of the Court
